QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_37

question.text: In the context of exit from an investee company, a 'put option' refers to:

answer.text: A right of the buyer of a security to sell it back to the seller per pre-agreed terms
An obligation to buy more shares if the company underperforms
A call option premium paid to the promoter

explanation.text: The Logic: A put option is a contractual right (but not an obligation) of the buyer of a security to sell the security back to the seller per pre-agreed terms. In the AIF context, the AIF can exercise the put on the promoter or the company for buyback. The Trap: Option B inverts right and obligation. Option C confuses a call premium with a put. Option D irrelevantly invokes Cat I/II tax provisions. Note: The put-option definition appears as a footnote in the workbook on p. 356, in the discussion of contractual exits from investee companies.
